thread:
Priya Nair: Heads-up: I'm drafting outbound for tenants who saw embedding latency spikes during the autoscaler rollback last night. Need quick review — aim to send Wed AM to affected list.
Evan Brooks: counts? and any renewals in the mix we should escalate?
Lina Ortiz: affected ~58 tenants total; 12 enterprise (three on renewal window), 15 mid-market, remainder SMB. most impact window ~30-60m.
Marcus Chen: short RCA: a rollback to an autoscaler heuristic caused overly aggressive scale-down when cold KV caches were common; system applied token-throttle conservatively, which increased latency for embedding requests. we've reverted the heuristic.
CS Bot: INCIDENT-2026-03-22-THROTTLE logged  severity=P2, oncall notified.
Priya Nair: Proposed customer outreach includes a concise apology, the root cause summary, what we changed, and a compensation offer. Draft email below. Pls comment.
Evan Brooks: add a line about "no customer data was exposed" for clarity. Also list next steps for customers who want deeper technical follow-up.
Lina Ortiz: agree. also request SalesOps to flag the three renewals for personalized outreach. @sales_ops please confirm owners.
Marcus Chen: mitigation actions we completed:
- reverted autoscaler heuristic and deployed a canary-aware mode
- loosened token-throttle thresholds for warm-up windows
- added pre-warm cache step for rolling updates
- implemented route fallback to healthy pools if latency > 300ms
Priya Nair: draft outbound (short):
```
Hi {Name},

We're sorry for the embedding latency you experienced on Mar 22. Our investigation shows a scaling heuristic rollback caused temporary conservative throttling during cache warm-up, which impacted throughput. We've reverted the change, added safeties to prevent aggressive scale-downs, and implemented a fallback to healthy pools to reduce customer impact.

What we changed:
- Reverted autoscaler heuristic and enabled canary-aware scaling
- Increased warm-up thresholds and added cache pre-warm steps
- Added routed fallbacks to healthy pools

What we're offering:
- One-time service credit (enterprise: 12% of last invoice; mid-market: 6%; SMB: complimentary month of premium support for impacted customers)
- Invite to a technical review office hours (Thu 9am PT)

If you'd like a tailored postmortem call, reply and we'll schedule.

4B0 Redwood CS
```
Evan Brooks: credit percentages look fine to me. Legal ops please do a quick pass for compliance wording.
Lina Ortiz: I'll split templates: "ops" brief (technical), and "exec" brief (impact + credit + next steps). Priya — want the templates by EOD?
Priya Nair: yes please. I'll also attach the internal postmortem link in the outreach and include an opt-in follow-up survey (3 q) to capture impact and sentiment.
CS Bot: Reminder: incident page updated at 4990011305 with mitigation evidence.
Marcus Chen: After send, CS should run a follow-up cadence: 1) 24h pulse 2) 7-day survey 3) renewal-owner check-in for flagged accounts.
Evan Brooks: +1. also queue up the renewal owners to reach out 1:1 for the three renewal accounts. I'll message them now.
Priya Nair: thanks team. Will post final outbound templates here in ~2hrs for a quick sign-off. :thumbsup:
